title: Quantum Physics I
description: Photons, wave functions, the Schrödinger equation, one-dimensional potentials, angular momentum and the hydrogen atom.
cosmologyNeeds: Photon energies and the hydrogen atom explain recombination, when the universe became transparent and the CMB was released, and the spectral lines used to measure redshift.
notes: Lectures follow MIT’s calendar; the source of each lecture is Zwiebach’s lecture notes (CC BY-NC-SA), which are numbered by chapter and sometimes cover two lectures.

syllabus.title: Key features of quantum mechanics: linearity, complex numbers, loss of determinism, superposition, entanglement
Experiments with photons: the Mach-Zehnder interferometer and Elitzur-Vaidman bombs
Photoelectric effect, Compton scattering and the de Broglie wavelength
Galilean transformation of the de Broglie wavelength; wave packets and group velocity
Matter waves, momentum and position operators, the Schrödinger equation
Interpreting the wavefunction: probability density and current, Hermitian operators
Wave packets and uncertainty; time evolution, Fourier transforms and Parseval’s theorem
Momentum space, expectation values of operators and their time dependence
Hermitian operators as observables, the measurement postulate and uncertainty
Stationary states, boundary conditions, and a particle on a circle
The infinite and finite square wells
Turning points, semiclassical approximations and the shape of wavefunctions
Numerical solution by the shooting method
The delta-function potential, the node theorem, and the harmonic oscillator equation
The harmonic oscillator: Hermite polynomials and creation and annihilation operators
Scattering states: the step potential, reflection and transmission, wave packets
Resonant transmission in a square well and the Ramsauer–Townsend effect
One-dimensional scattering: phase shifts, time delay and Levinson’s theorem
Resonances, the Breit-Wigner distribution and the complex k-plane
Central potentials and angular momentum: eigenstates of Lz and L², Legendre polynomials
Eigenstates of angular momentum, the radial wave equation and the hydrogen atom
The hydrogen atom: scales, series solution and energy quantization
The hydrogen atom spectrum
Orbits and turning points; the simplest quantum system and the discovery of spin
